text:
Alex: Heads up — saw 3 late telemetry batches from eu-west yesterday that blocked the main recompute wave. Thinking we need a staggered handoff + preemption rules instead of the current all-or-nothing. Thoughts?
Maria: +1 on staggered handoff. Can we avoid touching the console UX too much? ideally this is policy-only first.
Chris: What metrics are we targeting to decide preemption? latency SLA or shard age? quota consumption will spike if we preempt badly.
Priya: Suggestion: use shard_age (hours since last successful aggregate) + job_type (delta vs full) to compute a priority score. Delta-only backfills get a soft-priority bump but cannot evict a running recompute unless score delta > X.
Sam: Implementation note — replayer currently accepts `priority` but not a `handoff_to` routing key. Adding `handoff_to: low-memory-pool` + `checkpoint_id` lets operator move a job without losing progress. Example:```json
{
  "job_id": "r-2026-03-19-42",
  "priority": 120,
  "handoff_to": "preemptible-batch",
  "checkpoint_id": "cp-9876"
}```
Maria: That `handoff_to` header makes sense. How do we surface it in the console? a small toggle on the backfill run page?
Alex: For console, prefer: keep UI minimal. Expose "Allow preemption" checkbox and a non-editable computed priority score. Advanced users can use the API to set `handoff_to`.
Chris: Also need quota guardrails — if preemption moves N jobs into preemptible pool we should cap concurrent preemptibles per org to avoid noisy neighbor. Put it behind the quota service.
Priya: Agreed. Quota rule: preemptible_slots_per_org = min(10, floor(commit_level/100GB)). If exceeded, new handoffs are queued instead of forced.
replay-bot: queue_update: moved 2 jobs -> preemptible-batch (r-2026-03-19-42, r-2026-03-19-43) by Alex
Sam: Ops checklist for the code change: 1) add `handoff_to` to replay API, 2) persist `checkpoint_id` and resume logic, 3) add quota checks in scheduler, 4) telemetry events for handoff decision (why evicted, score, org).
Alex: Can we canary this in staging with a tiny tenant cohort? I want to validate aggregate correctness after resumes.
deploy-bot: rollout: replay-service v1.12.0-staging deployed to staging cluster at 2026-03-19T15:12Z :sparkles:
Maria: After staging, we'll need a quick smoke: run 5 small backfills and 2 recompute waves that overlap. Check aggregated counts + idempotency.
Chris: One open API debate: should `priority` be an integer that operators manipulate, or read-only computed from policy and only overrideable via an `override_reason` field? I vote policy-computed by default, manual overrides require audit log.
Priya: Override with audit log please. Security + compliance asks for who/why. Add `override_reason` and `override_by` to job metadata.
Sam: I'll add `override_*` fields and wire the audit events. Also will emit a `handoff_decision` telemetry event with `score_components` so console can show a tooltip like "Why this job was preempted".
Alex: OK plan: Sam implements API+scheduler changes, Priya updates quota rules, Maria prepares minimal console toggle + tooltip copy, Chris writes staging smoke tests and failure cases, I'll coordinate oncall handoff doc and runbook. Can we aim to merge by EOD Friday and canary next week?
Maria: Sounds good. I'll add the console PR draft and copy for the tooltip. Link to draft: https://go.redwood/replay-handoff-console-draft
Chris: I'll write the smoke test harness, include a randomized resume/shutdown scenario to catch checkpoint bugs.
Priya: I'll update quota service and add unit tests for preemptible slot accounting.
Sam: I'll open the replay-service PR and tag everyone for review.
Alex: Thanks — if no objections we ship the minimal policy-first change to staging. We'll keep manual overrides audit-locked.
Maria: :thumbsup:
replay-bot: scheduled_run: canary cohort (orgs: 5) queued at 2026-03-19T16:00Z
Alex: Closing here — followups in PR threads and the staging run.
